original_post_text:
Shuffle $100k Series recap — 5 bullets, $150 each. 
$750 invested. One min cash that returned $250. 

Net: -$500.

That’s poker. No shame in it.

But here’s how I look at it: I’m not a tournament-to-tournament grinder. For players who go hard every single week chasing big fields, tournament variance can be absolutely brutal on your bankroll and your mindset. I’ve seen it. I respect the dedication, but that’s not my game plan.

My next move is back to cash games. A solid week of grinding $1/$2, $1/$3, $2/$5 and that $500 is very easily recovered, with profit on top. That’s how you keep poker manageable and repeatable.

And honestly? It’s only 6 PM. The night is young. I might make that $500 back tonight.

#ShamGodPoker #DFWPoker #PokerLifestyle

expanded_body:
Originally posted March 13–14, 2026.

Walked into Shuffle 214 on Friday night with $100,000 on the line — Flight 1H at 6 PM on Friday, March 13, followed by Saturday's Flight 1I at 11 AM and Flight 1J at 6 PM. Call a $150 buy-in a donation if you want; going in, I called it an investment.

Here's the final ledger:
• Event: Shuffle 214 $100K GTD Series
• Bullets fired: 5 entries at $150 each
• Total invested: $750
• Return: 1 min-cash for $250
• Net result: -$500

That's poker. No shame in it.

But here's how I look at it: I'm not a tournament-to-tournament grinder. For players who go hard every single week chasing big fields, tournament variance can be absolutely brutal on your bankroll and your mindset. I've seen it. I respect the dedication, but that's not my game plan.

My next move is back to cash games. A solid week of grinding $1/$2, $1/$3, and $2/$5 and that $500 is very easily recovered, with profit on top. That's how you keep poker manageable and repeatable.

And honestly? When I wrapped the tournament at 6 PM, the night was still young.

— Sham
